title: An fppf covering has an integral surjection with open local lifts
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] in the universes [def-weil-size-convention], and let $\{f_i:X_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ be a small fppf covering [def-pc-fppf-site]: every $f_i$ is flat and locally of finite presentation and the family is jointly surjective. There exist an integral morphism $q:Y\to X$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] which is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism], a small open covering $Y=\bigcup_{\alpha\in A}W_\alpha$ [def-weil-open-immersion], indices $i(\alpha)\in I$, and $X$-morphisms $h_\alpha:W_\alpha\to X_{i(\alpha)}$, so $f_{i(\alpha)}\circ h_\alpha=q|_{W_\alpha}$. There is no quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness assumption on $X$, and no finiteness or finite-presentation assertion about $q$. The empty scheme and the empty covering are allowed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-fppf-local-finite-free-refinement] to the given fppf covering. We obtain a Zariski cover $X=\bigcup_jU_j$, surjective finite locally free maps $W_j\to U_j$, open covers $W_j=\bigcup_kW_{j,k}$, and surjective finite locally free maps $T_{j,k}\to W_{j,k}$, with each composite $T_{j,k}\to X$ factoring through one member $X_i\to X$.

By [lem-trf-integral-surjective-open-extension], extend each surjective integral map $W_j\to U_j$ to a surjective integral map $\overline W_j\to X$, and extend each surjective integral map $T_{j,k}\to W_{j,k}$ to a surjective integral map $\overline T_{j,k}\to\overline W_j$. The open inverse images agree with the original schemes over $U_j$ and $W_{j,k}$, respectively.

For each $j$ take the product $\overline T_j=\prod_k\overline T_{j,k}$ over $\overline W_j$, and then take $Y=\prod_j\overline T_j$ over $X$. The products exist by [lem-trf-affine-infinite-product-existence], because integral morphisms are affine by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Each $\overline T_j\to\overline W_j$ is integral and surjective by [lem-trf-infinite-product-integral] and [lem-trf-infinite-product-surjective]. Its composite $\overline T_j\to X$ is integral and surjective by [lem-trf-integral-morphism-composition] and [lem-trf-surjective-morphism-composition]. Applying the same two product lemmas to the family $\overline T_j\to X$ shows that $q:Y\to X$ is integral and surjective.

For every $j,k$, let $W_{j,k}'\subset Y$ be the inverse image of the open $T_{j,k}\subset\overline T_{j,k}$ under the projection $Y\to\overline T_j\to\overline T_{j,k}$. These opens cover $Y$: if $y\in Y$, its image in $X$ lies in some $U_j$, its image in $\overline W_j$ lies in some $W_{j,k}$, and then its image in $\overline T_{j,k}$ lies in the inverse image of $W_{j,k}$, namely $T_{j,k}$. The projection therefore gives an $X$-morphism $W_{j,k}'\to T_{j,k}$, and the factorization from Step 1 gives a lift $W_{j,k}'\to X_i$ for some $i$. Thus these opens form the required small open covering and local lifts. This is the pointwise argument in Tag 0CNZ; openness is preserved by inverse image of an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion].

If $X$ is empty, the identity of $X$ with the empty open covering supplies the conclusion; if the original indexing family is empty, joint surjectivity forces $X$ to be empty. The constructions above also allow empty index sets under the size convention [def-weil-size-convention]. No quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, finiteness, or finite-presentation hypothesis on $X$ or on $q$ has been introduced.
